title: wringer.readiness.v1
description: Each credential lane in one word, as a record, written by wringer-drive beside the journey BEFORE anything is spent (0.9.9, SOTA item 5). Run 5 (2026-09-05) confirmed the readiness card's prose was honest about a displaced login; this makes the classification a typed fact the card quotes and a reader can check, so that 'Ready' can never mean 'a variable was found and we hope it works'. Derived from WorkerAuth's typed facts and doctor's drafting-key check — never from their prose. The drafting lane is never `verified`: Wringer never probes the drafting endpoint for free.

word.description: ONE of the words a lane may be. `verified` is the vendor's own free answer that it is logged in with no key displacing that login — and only that; a present key is not a valid one, and neither is a login the vendor says it made WITH a key (`authMethod: api_key`). `displaced` is a key over a stored login (run 4B's trap). `declared-unverified` is a key that is set — in the environment, or named by the vendor as what authenticated it — and nothing that has said it works. `unavailable` is the vendor's own word that it is logged out, with no key to fall back on. `not-applicable` is the engine's own word for a shell worker with no login surface on the roster. `unmeasured` is the second word the engine adds for the same reason: a probe that could not be run or could not be read, a containment, a config that would not parse — nobody could tell, and a silence must not read as a declaration or a refusal.

detail.description: The engine's own sentence for the lane — doctor's check or the worker's auth reading — verbatim.
